Three acrobatic performers try to hold their ground, literally and figuratively, while the ground beneath their feet keeps shifting. To remain standing, they constantly have to adapt. Running, tumbling, dashing, they try to stay on their feet.

They cling to each other, to an edge, or to a spectator’s hand. With the audience all around them and bathed in compelling electronic music, the performers try to find a new balance between the flying, sliding, falling and catching.

Should they strive for control? Or perhaps learn to stagger really well? The musical circus theatre SKRAM pays tribute to resilience. A tribute to the courage to stagger, take risks, fail and get back up again.

What do you do when you feel like everything is constantly rushing past you? Boom. What if you can hear the muffled bass, but have no clue where it’s coming from? Boom, boom. What if life feels like a great, thumping party that you just can’t find the entrance to? Boom, boom, boom.

How long will you keep searching in that cold and deserted industrial estate? And are all those exuberant others really there, or are they just ghosts in your head?

Theater Artemis' played at the Edinburgh International Children’s Festival in May, read the reviews by Everything Theatre , The QR and Corr Blimey .

What does it mean to live? A philosopher, a child and an adult set off on a journey with this question. The stage is empty. And yet the philosopher and the child keep seeing undiscovered landscapes and mysterious animals and life forms: wolves, bacteria, olive trees, polar bears, etc. Their curiosity is too great not to follow in their footsteps.

But for the adult following them, the stage is truly empty, and animals have long since ceased to inhabit his mind and nights. What sort of game is this, he wonders. Do they really mean this? Hesitantly, he accepts the invitation to enter the world of the philosopher and the child and to set his mind (and ours) free.

Tg STAN’s leading figure Jolente De Keersmaeker and French choreographer Jérôme Bel created Recommencer ce monde in 2024, in collaboration with French art historian Estelle Zhong Mengual, a French-language production based on the work of contemporary French philosopher Baptiste Morizot. De Wereld Herbeginnen is now the Dutch-language version of this work.

I’ve learned to tell stories. Thanks to her, I know: stories help. Stories are to the mind what breath is to the lungs. A brother and a sister. The brother is 12 and plays battle games online, where it’s a matter of life and death. He can always come back to life. But his sister, Nour, is ill and has no additional lives. She’s barely going to make it to her seventh birthday. To distract her, the brother tells her stories. Nour wants to know what it’s like to be ‘grown up’, so through his stories the brother imagines a future life for her. He lets her fly the nest, meet a boy, experience her first crush and her first heartache.

Can he lull his sister to sleep with a story and promise that he’ll never forget her?

In poetic language and with the necessary dose of gentle humour, Elvis Peeters and Nicole Van Bael wrote the novella Wat alleen wij weten . De Roovers are bringing this story to the stage. Through the craft of shadow play, an ancient theatrical tradition, they attempt to grapple with the contradiction of life and death and the fading of memories.

During the spring half-term holidays, hetpaleis, together with Youth Film Festival Antwerp, invites you to go on a cinematic theatre trip.

For five days, you’ll discover the world of film and theatre. On the programme? Everything about storytelling. Yes, absolutely EVERYTHING. You’ll learn about camera angles, special effects and stop motion. You’ll learn what the differences and similarities are and how to tell a good story.

With your camera in hand, you’ll capture footage and build your own animated world in which you’ll also star. After this week, no story will be safe.

Macy knows a lot. She knows the names of the oceans, she knows the seasons, she knows the names of birds. But as for what happened between her father and mother, she can only guess. So Macy makes up her own version.

Wat Macy weet is about what mothers and fathers say when they no longer know themselves, stories to fill the void, being someone else week after week and the importance of knowing where you stand.

Femke Heijens ( HUGS ) directs Hélène Devos in a monologue about a sensitive daughter of divorced parents. Angelo Tijssens (co-screenwriter of, among others, Close ) is behind the script, loosely based on Henry James’s What Maisie Knew (1897), a novel about a girl who, following her parents’ divorce, lives alternately with her father and mother while trying to take control of her own life. She takes on their roles and tries to understand the world through play.
